subject: Airgapization of inference planes — Dedicated & Private topology review and evidence checklist

From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@veridian.com>

Cc: security@veridian.com, gcp-cloud-arch@veridian.com

Subject: Inquiry: architecture for isolated inference planes (Dedicated & Private)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of Veridian's SOC 2 scoping and our SIG questionnaire, we need a clear architecture description and evidence for how Redwood can provide an "air-gapped" or strongly isolated inference plane for regulated models.

High-level asks:
- A topology diagram showing control plane separation vs data plane for both Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.
- A short narrative describing how we achieve logical and (optionally) physical isolation, KMS boundaries, and egress controls.
- Evidence artifacts we can attach to the SIG: firewall rules, VPC peering configs, and examples of network ACLs or iptables snippets.

We'd like something that our security team can include in the SIG and CAIQ responses — ideally labelled so we can reference specific sections. Can you provide a short package and a checklist of items we can hold as evidence?

Best,
Alice
Alice Morris
Senior InfoSec Manager | Veridian Systems
security@veridian.com

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@veridian.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-27T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Inquiry: architecture for isolated inference planes (Dedicated & Private)

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Attaching an initial topology image and a short evidence summary (attached as v1) for review. High-level notes below; fuller artifact bundle to follow by EOD Friday (PST).

Summary (short):
- Two inference planes: 
  1) Dedicated plane: single-tenant GPU pools with tenant-aware routing. Network isolation at the VPC/subnet level plus dedicated KMS key per account. Optional private peering into customer VPC (no public egress required).
  2) Private plane (VPC/on-prem): control plane runs in Redwood-managed Control VPC, customer data path is routed over private peering or customer-managed interconnect, with an option for an on-prem inference enclave (air-gapped) where the customer controls physical access.

- Control plane separation: control plane (management/orchestration) communicates with inference nodes over authenticated mTLS channels via a dedicated control-net that does not traverse customer data paths. Control plane logs are stored in a separate encrypted bucket with restricted roles.

- KMS/crypto boundaries: we recommend a customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated when required; keys never leave the customer KMS. For hosted customers we use Redwood KMS with strict access controls and audit logs.

- Egress & data exfiltration mitigations: egress gateways and explicit allowlists per deployment; default deny for all outbound except telemetry endpoints that are documented and auditable. For air-gapped setups we provide an offline bundle for model artifacts and an out-of-band management channel.

Next steps we propose: 1) quick 30-min review call with your security and GCP architects, 2) deliver labeled evidence pack (firewall snippets, sample iptables, peering configs, KMS policy examples, and the topology diagram).

Attachments (v1): dedicated_private_plane_topology_v1.png, segregation_evidence_summary_v2.pdf (redacted), network_rule_snippets.txt

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Fri, Aug 27, 2026 at 6:03 PM rishi_malhotra@redwood.com wrote:
> Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Attaching an initial topology image and a short evidence summary (attached as v1) for review. High-level notes below; fuller artifact bundle to follow by EOD Friday (PST).
>
> Summary (short):
> - Two inference planes: 
>   1) Dedicated plane: single-tenant GPU pools with tenant-aware routing. Network isolation at the VPC/subnet level plus dedicated KMS key per account. Optional private peering into customer VPC (no public egress required).
>   2) Private plane (VPC/on-prem): control plane runs in Redwood-managed Control VPC, customer data path is routed over private peering or customer-managed interconnect, with an option for an on-prem inference enclave (air-gapped) where the customer controls physical access.

Adding technical detail for the evidence pack:
- Network segmentation: We use separate Kubernetes clusters and separate subnet ranges per tenant for Dedicated. Network policies (Calico) block pod-to-pod across tenant subnets; cluster egress flows are forced through an egress proxy appliance (envoy-based) where we can apply filtering and logging.
- For Private (VPC): we supply a validated Terraform module for peerings and a sample route table that explicitly pins traffic to customer VPN/HA interconnect. For on-prem air-gapped enclaves we provide a signed manifest of allowed binaries and a hash list for model artifacts.
- Sample artifacts included in the pack: 
  * iptables fragments showing drop/allow rules;
  * sample VPC route table export;
  * KMS key policy example showing only the customer principal + a restricted Redwood service principal with "Encrypt/Decrypt" limited to usage in the inference subnet.

Karthik — can you confirm which of the SOC 2 evidence items we already have in the central evidence vault (audit logs, key rotation records, control plane runbooks) so we can mark them in the checklist?

Kimberly Park
Director, Cloud Security 
Redwood Inference

Alice — attaching the labeled evidence bundle you can ingest into your SIG/CAIQ response. Bundle contents (high level):
- Topology image: dedicated_private_plane_topology_v1.png (annotated with control vs data paths, optional airgap points).
- Segregation evidence summary (PDF): sections map to SIG/CAIQ control IDs, includes links to artifacts we can share under NDA.
- Network rule snippets (txt): iptables/Calico fragments and an example egress proxy config.
- Artifact index: maps each artifact to the SOC 2 category (CC6.1, CC7.1 etc.) and notes whether the artifact is Redwood-managed or customer-managed.

Quick checklist for ingestion into your SIG answers (copyable):
1) Topology diagram labeled with ControlPlane-1 and DataPlane-1 (attached).
2) KMS boundary: customer-managed KMS recommended for Private/Dedicated. Example KMS policy included (network_rule_snippets.txt).
3) Egress controls: egress gateway configuration and default-deny policy documented (segregation_evidence_summary_v2.pdf).
4) Audit logs: link to centralized audit logs and retention policy (we will share a redacted export under NDA).
5) Binary & model artifact signing: manifest and hash list for air-gapped setups (included in evidence summary).

If this looks good, we'll prepare the redacted evidence exports and an access plan (DocuSign/NDA) so you can attach them to the SIG portal. Would you like the team to join a 30-min walkthrough with your security and GCP architects tomorrow?

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
